source_fields.label: pneumocystosis
source_fields.definition: Human pneumocystosis is caused by an infectious agent, which (after recent nomenclature and taxonomy revisions) is now classed as the fungus Pneumocystis jiroveci. The prevalence is unknown. Pneumocystis jiroveci is an opportunistic infectious agent, developing in immunosuppressed patients. It is an air-borne infection, localized to the lungs. However, extrapulmonary involvement is seen in AIDS patients. The disease manifests progressively with coughing, respiratory problems (dyspnea) and fever, followed by acute respiratory insufficiency and death within a few weeks in untreated cases. The most reliable diagnostic method is bronchoalveolar lavage. The treatment of choice is cotrimoxazole.

source_fields.label: systemic sclerosis
source_fields.definition: A chronic disorder, possibly autoimmune, marked by excessive production of collagen which results in hardening and thickening of body tissues. The two types of systemic scleroderma, limited cutaneous and diffuse cutaneous are classified with focus on the extent of affected skin. A relationship exists between the extent of skin area affected and degree of internal organ/system involvement. Systemic scleroderma can manifest itself in pulmonary fibrosis, Raynaud's syndrome, digestive system telangiectasias, renal hypertension and/or pulmonary hypertension.

source_fields.label: localized scleroderma
source_fields.definition: Localized scleroderma is the skin localized form of scleroderma characterized by fibrosis of the skin causing cutaneous plaques or strips.

display_name: X-linked intellectual disability with isolated growth hormone deficiency

source_fields.label: X-linked intellectual disability with isolated growth hormone deficiency
obsolete hereditary late onset Parkinson disease
interstitial cystitis
source_fields.definition: A rare chronic debilitating urogenital disease characterized by urinary frequency, urgency, and pelvic pain.

source_fields.label: verrucous hemangioma
source_fields.definition: A skin hemangioma characterized by the presence of epidermal hyperplasia.

source_fields.label: legionellosis
source_fields.definition: Any disease caused by Legionella bacteria.

source_fields.label: leprosy
source_fields.definition: Leprosy is a chronic infectious disease affecting primarily the skin and peripheral nervous system.
synonyms: Mycobacterium leprae caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: follicular lymphoma
source_fields.definition: Follicular lymphoma is a form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by a proliferation of B cells whose nodular structure of follicular architecture is preserved.

source_fields.label: Lyell syndrome
source_fields.definition: Lyell syndrome is an extended form of toxic epidermal necrolysis characterized by destruction and detachment of the skin epithelium and mucous membranes involving more than 30% of the body surface area.

display_name: familial papillary or follicular thyroid carcinoma

source_fields.label: familial papillary or follicular thyroid carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A papillary or follicular thyroid gland carcinoma with a genetic component that develops within the same family. Current studies suggest that it is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. It is often multifocal and bilateral and usually affects younger patients.

source_fields.label: listeriosis
source_fields.definition: A bacterial infection caused by Listeria monocytogenes. It occurs in newborns, elderly, and immunocompromised patients. The bacteria are transmitted through ingestion of contaminated food. Clinical manifestations include fever, muscle pain, respiratory distress, nausea, diarrhea, neck stiffness, irritability, seizures, and lethargy.
synonyms: Listeria monocytogenes caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: necrotizing enterocolitis
source_fields.definition: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating disease that affects mostly the intestine of premature infants. The wall of the intestine is invaded by bacteria, which cause local infection and inflammation that can ultimately destroy the wall of the bowel (intestine). Such bowel wall destruction can lead to perforation of the intestine and spillage of stool into the infant's abdomen, which can result in an overwhelming infection and death.
synonyms: necrotizing enterocolitis in fetus or newborn
necrotizing enterocolitis in foetus or newborn

source_fields.label: leptospirosis
source_fields.definition: A contagious bacterial infection caused by spirochetes of the genus Leptospira. Humans are infected by contact with water and soil which have been contaminated with animal waste products. The signs and symptoms include an initial flu-like phase, followed by a second phase in which patients may develop meningitis, liver failure and renal failure.

source_fields.label: narcolepsy-cataplexy syndrome
source_fields.definition: A type of narcolepsy characterized by excessive day-time sleepiness associated with uncontrollable sleep urges and cataplexy (loss of muscle tone often triggered by pleasant emotions).

source_fields.label: Berardinelli-Seip congenital lipodystrophy
source_fields.definition: A lipodystrophy characterized by the association of lipoatrophy, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatomegaly and acromegaloid features. BSCL belongs to the group of extreme insulin resistance syndromes, which also includes leprechaunism, Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome, acquired generalized lipodystrophy, and types A and B insulin resistance.

source_fields.label: rat-bite fever
source_fields.definition: An infectious disease that is caused transmitted by the bite of a rat. Two species of bacteria can cause the infection: Streptobacillus moniliformis and Spirillum minus.

source_fields.label: tularemia
source_fields.definition: Tularemia is an infection caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis. It is more common in rodents and rabbits but has been found in other animals including domestic cats, sheep, birds, and hamsters. Humans can become infected in several different ways: by handling infected animals, through tick or deer fly bites, by drinking contaminated water, or by inhaling contaminated dust or aerosols. Person-to-person transmission has not been reported. The type of tularemia and the particular signs and symptoms vary depending on how the bacteria enter the body. However, fever is seen in most cases. Though tularemia can be life-threatening, most infections can be treated with antibiotics.
synonyms: Francisella tularensis caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: melioidosis
source_fields.definition: An infection that is caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, which is found in soil and water; symptoms vary widely, but most commonly include fever, cough, pneumonia, arthralgia, myalgia, and skin ulceration.
synonyms: Burkholderia pseudomallei caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: nocardiosis
source_fields.definition: Nocardiosis is a local (skin, lung, brain) or disseminated (whole body) acute, subacute, or chronic bacterial infection.

source_fields.label: juvenile Huntington disease
source_fields.definition: Juvenile Huntington disease (JHD) is a form of Huntington disease (HD), characterized by onset of signs and symptoms before 20 years of age.

source_fields.label: congenital diaphragmatic hernia
source_fields.definition: A posterolateral defect of the diaphragm that allows passage of abdominal viscera into the thorax, leading to respiratory insufficiency and persistent pulmonary hypertension with high mortality.

source_fields.label: toxin-mediated infectious botulism
source_fields.definition: Aform of botulism (see this term), a rare acquired neuromuscular junction disease, characterized by descending flaccid paralysis caused by botulinum neurotoxins (BoNTs), produced in vivo leading to toxin-mediated infection. Infectious botulism includes wound botulism and intestinal toxemia botulism (infant botulism and adult intestinal botulism).

source_fields.label: growth hormone insensitivity syndrome
source_fields.definition: Growth hormone insensitivity syndrome (GHIS) is a group of diseases characterized by marked short stature associated with normal or elevated growth hormone (GH) concentrations, which fail to respond to exogenous GH administration. GHIS comprises growth delay due to IGF-1 deficiency, growth delay due to IGF-1 resistance, Laron syndrome, short stature due to STAT5b deficiency and primary acid-labile subunit (ALS) deficiency.
synonyms: short stature due to a defect in growth hormone receptor or post-receptor pathway

source_fields.label: glossopharyngeal neuralgia
source_fields.definition: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia is a condition characterized by repeated episodes of severe pain in the tongue, throat, ear, and tonsils (areas connected to the ninth cranial nerve, or glossopharyngeal nerve). It typically occurs in individuals over age 40. Episodes of pain may last from a few seconds to a few minutes, and usually occur on one side. The pain may be triggered by swallowing, speaking, laughing, chewing or coughing. The condition is thought to be due to irritation of the nerve, although the source of irritation is unclear. The goal of treatment is to control pain, but over-the-counter pain medications are not very effective; the most effective drugs are anti-seizure medications. Some antidepressants help certain people. Surgery to cut or take pressure off of the glossopharyngeal nerve may be needed in severe cases.

source_fields.label: infantile spasms
source_fields.definition: A rare epilepsy syndrome characterized by onset of epileptic spasms in infants between 2 and 12 months of age, and rarely up to 24 months. Infants may have no antecedent history, or a history reflecting the underlying cause. The classical triad of epileptic spasms, hypsarrhythmia and developmental stagnation or regression is historically referred to as West syndrome.
synonyms: tonic spasms with clustering, arrest of psychomotor development and hypsarrhythmia on EEG

source_fields.label: Whipple disease
source_fields.definition: A systemic infection caused by the Gram-positive bacterium Tropheryma whipplei. It affects the small intestine resulting in malabsorption. Other sites or systems affected by the infection are the joints, central nervous system, and the cardiovascular system.
synonyms: Tropheryma whipplei caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: acute interstitial pneumonia
source_fields.definition: Acute interstitial pneumonia (AIP), also referred to as Hamman-Rich syndrome, is a rapidly progressive and histologically distinct form of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia.

source_fields.label: retinal capillary malformation
source_fields.definition: Retinal cavernous hemangioma is a rare, benign, usually unilateral retinal vascular hamartoma that in most cases is asymptomatic but in some patients may present with blurred vision or floaters and that is characterized by the presence of grape-like vacuoles.

source_fields.label: neuromyelitis optica
source_fields.definition: A rare inflammatory disease of the central nervous system characterized mainly by attacks of uni- or bilateral optic neuritis (ON) and acute myelitis.

source_fields.label: beta-thalassemia intermedia
source_fields.definition: Beta-thalassemia (BT) intermedia is a form of BT characterized by mild to moderate anemia which does not or only occasionally requires transfusion.

source_fields.label: dominant beta-thalassemia
source_fields.definition: Dominant beta-thalassemia is a form of beta-thalassemia resulting in moderate to severe anemia.

source_fields.label: Kimura disease
source_fields.definition: Kimura disease is a benign and chronic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology, occurring mainly in Asian countries (very rarely in Western countries) and predominantly affecting young men, that usually presents with a solitary or multiple non-tender subcutaneous masses in the head and neck region (in particular the preauricular and submandibular area) and/or generalized painless lymphadenopathy, often with salivary gland involvement. Characteristic laboratory findings include blood eosinophilia and markedly elevated serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels. It is often associated with autoinflammatory disorders (i.e. ulcerative colitis, bronchial asthma) and a co-existing renal disease.

source_fields.label: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
source_fields.definition: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) is an autoimmune, presynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission characterized by fluctuating muscle weakness and autonomic dysfunction frequently associated with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC).

source_fields.label: granulomatous slack skin disease
source_fields.definition: Granulomatous slack skin (GSS) is a variant of mycosis fungoides (MF), a form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, and is characterized by the presence of circumscribed areas of pendulous lax skin.

source_fields.label: Kallmann syndrome
source_fields.definition: Kallmann syndrome (KS) is a developmental genetic disorder characterized by the association of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) due to gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) deficiency, and anosmia or hyposmia (with hypoplasia or aplasia of the olfactory bulbs).

source_fields.label: neuroleptic malignant syndrome
source_fields.definition: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is an idiosyncratic condition associated with administration of antipsychotic and other central dopaminergic blockers, and characterized by hyperthermia, muscular rigidity, autonomic dysfunction and altered consciousness.

source_fields.label: malignant hyperthermia of anesthesia
source_fields.definition: A pharmacogenetic disorder of skeletal muscle that presents as a hypermetabolic response to potent volatile anesthetic gasses such as halothane, sevoflurane, desflurane and the depolarizing muscle relaxant succinylcholine, and rarely, to stresses such as vigorous exercise and heat.

display_name: urinary bladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma

source_fields.label: urinary bladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A highly aggressive carcinoma, histologically resembling small cell lung carcinoma. In most cases it is associated with carcinoma in situ.
synonyms: poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma of the bladder
small cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder
small cell carcinoma of urinary bladder
small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the urinary bladder
small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of urinary bladder

source_fields.label: typhoid fever
source_fields.definition: A bacterial infectious disorder contracted by consumption of food or drink contaminated with Salmonella typhi. This disorder is common in developing countries and can be treated with antibiotics.

source_fields.label: calciphylaxis
source_fields.definition: Calciphylaxis is a disease in which blood vessels (veins and arteries) become blocked by a build-up of calcium in the walls of the vessels, preventing blood from flowing to the skin or internal organs. The lack of blood flow (ischemia) damages healthy tissue and causes itto die (necrosis). The most obvious and frequent symptom of calciphylaxis is damage to the skin, as ulcers can developand become infected easily. Calciphylaxis can also affect fat tissue, internal organs, and skeletal muscle, causing infections, pain, and organ failure.These symptoms are often irreversible, and many individuals with calciphylaxis may not survive more thana few months after they are diagnosed due to infection that spreads throughout the body (sepsis), or organ failure. The exact cause of calciphylaxis is unknown. Treatments may include medications to reduce pain, antibiotics to treat infections, and various approaches to preventing the development or worsening of this condition.

source_fields.label: pyoderma gangrenosum
source_fields.definition: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) is a primarily sterile inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis characterized by recurrent cutaneous ulcerations with a mucopurulent or hemorrhagic exudate.

source_fields.label: pituicytoma
source_fields.definition: An extremely rare, WHO grade I, circumscribed and slow-growing tumor that arises from the neurohypophysis or infundibulum and described in adults. It is characterized by the presence of elongated, spindle-shaped neoplastic glial cells that form storiform patterns or interlacing fascicular arrangements. Signs and symptoms include visual disturbances, headache, amenorrhea, and decreased libido.

source_fields.label: preeclampsia
source_fields.definition: Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that is characterized by new-onset hypertension with proteinuria presenting after 20 weeks of gestation, and depending on mild or severe forms may initially present with severe headache, visual disturbances, and hyperreflexia.

source_fields.label: pituitary gigantism
source_fields.definition: The condition of accelerated and excessive growth in children or adolescents who are exposed to excess human growth hormone before the closure of epiphyses. It is usually caused by somatotroph hyperplasia or a growth hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma. These patients are of abnormally tall stature, more than 3 standard deviations above normal mean height for age.
synonyms: infantile and juvenile forms of acromegaly

source_fields.label: scrub typhus
source_fields.definition: Scrub typhus is a rare dust mite-borne infectious disease caused by the Orientia tsutsugamushi bacterium and characterized clinically by an eruptive fever which is potentially serious.

source_fields.label: boutonneuse fever
source_fields.definition: An infectious disease of the Mediterranean area, the Crimea, Africa, and India, caused by infection with rickettsia conorii subsp. coronorii.
synonyms: tick typhus due to rickettsia conorii

source_fields.label: autosomal erythropoietic protoporphyria
source_fields.definition: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is an inherited disorder of the heme metabolic pathway characterized by accumulation of protoporphyrin in blood, erythrocytes and tissues, and cutaneous manifestations of photosensitivity.

source_fields.label: scotoma
source_fields.definition: A localized defect in the visual field bordered by an area of normal vision. This occurs with a variety of eye diseases (e.g., retinal diseases and glaucoma); optic nerve diseases, and other conditions.
synonyms: generalised visual field contraction or constriction

source_fields.label: corneal ulcer
source_fields.definition: Area of epithelial tissue loss from corneal surface; associated with inflammatory cells in the cornea and anterior chamber.

source_fields.label: psychotic disorder
source_fields.definition: An abnormal condition of the mind that involves a loss of contact with reality. People experiencing psychosis may exhibit personality changes and thought disorder. Depending on its severity, this may be accompanied by unusual or bizarre behavior, as well as difficulty with social interaction and impairment in carrying out daily life activities.

source_fields.label: amenorrhea
source_fields.definition: The absence of menses in a woman who has achieved reproductive age.

source_fields.label: diabetes mellitus
source_fields.definition: A metabolic disorder characterized by abnormally high blood sugar levels due to diminished production of insulin or insulin resistance/desensitization.

source_fields.label: thyroiditis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the thyroid gland. This category includes Hashimoto thyroiditis, Riedel thyroiditis, acute thyroiditis, subacute thyroiditis, and radiation-induced thyroiditis.

source_fields.label: hypertensive disorder
source_fields.definition: Persistently high systemic arterial blood pressure. Based on multiple readings (blood pressure determination), hypertension is currently defined as when systolic pressure is consistently greater than 140 mm Hg or when diastolic pressure is consistently 90 mm Hg or more.

source_fields.label: hypopigmentation of the skin
source_fields.definition: A condition caused by a deficiency or a loss of melanin pigmentation in the epidermis, also known as hypomelanosis. Hypopigmentation can be localized or generalized, and may result from genetic defects, trauma, inflammation, or infections.

source_fields.label: conjunctivitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye.

source_fields.label: adrenal gland hyperfunction
source_fields.definition: Excess production of adrenal cortex hormones.

source_fields.label: atrioventricular block
source_fields.definition: A heart block that is initiated in the atrioventricular node.

source_fields.label: osteomyelitis
source_fields.definition: An acute or chronic inflammation of the bone and its structures due to infection with pyogenic bacteria.

source_fields.label: polycythemia
source_fields.definition: Abnormally high mass or concentration of red blood cells in the blood, either due to an increase in erythropoiesis or a decrease in plasma volume.

source_fields.label: amyloidosis
source_fields.definition: A disorder characterized by the localized or diffuse accumulation of amyloid protein in various anatomic sites. It may be primary, due to clonal plasma cell proliferations; secondary, due to long standing infections, chronic inflammatory disorders, or malignancies; or familial. It may affect the nerves, skin, tongue, joints, heart, liver, spleen, kidneys and adrenal glands.

source_fields.label: acidosis disorder
source_fields.definition: An abnormally high acidity of the blood and other body tissues. Acidosis can be either respiratory or metabolic.

source_fields.label: obesity disorder
source_fields.definition: A disorder involving an excessive amount of body fat.

source_fields.label: diarrheal disease
source_fields.definition: The condition of having at least three loose or liquid bowel movements each day.

source_fields.label: aspiration pneumonia
source_fields.definition: A type of lung inflammation resulting from the aspiration of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

source_fields.label: pneumothorax
source_fields.definition: Abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity.

source_fields.label: stroke disorder
source_fields.definition: A sudden loss of neurological function secondary to hemorrhage or ischemia in the brain parenchyma due to a vascular event.

source_fields.label: arteriovenous hemangioma/malformation
source_fields.definition: A benign vascular lesion characterized by the presence of a complex network of communicating arterial and venous vascular structures.

source_fields.label: arteriosclerosis disorder
source_fields.definition: A vascular disorder characterized by thickening and hardening of the walls of the arteries.

source_fields.label: hypotensive disorder
source_fields.definition: Blood pressure that is abnormally low.

source_fields.label: megaloblastic anemia
source_fields.definition: Anemia characterized by the presence of unusually large erythroblasts in the bone marrow called megaloblasts. It is usually caused by vitamin B12 or folic acid deficiency. Other causes include toxins and drugs.

source_fields.label: obsolete rhabdomyolysis
source_fields.definition: OBSOLETE. A clinical syndrome resulting from direct or indirect muscle injury and subsequent release of myoglobin into the plasma.

source_fields.label: hypertrichosis
source_fields.definition: Excessive hair growth anywhere on the body.

source_fields.label: atrial fibrillation
source_fields.definition: A disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of a supraventricular arrhythmia characterized by the replacement of consistent P waves by rapid oscillations or fibrillatory waves that vary in size, shape and timing and are accompanied by an irregular ventricular response. (CDISC)

source_fields.label: mitral valve prolapse
source_fields.definition: A fairly common and often benign valvular heart disorder characterized by redundancy or hooding of mitral valve leaflets so that they prolapse into the left atrium, often causing mitral regurgitation. It is often a symptomless condition but may be marked by varied symptoms (e.g. chest pain, fatigue, dizziness, dyspnea, or palpitations) leading in some cases to endocarditis or ventricular tachycardia.

source_fields.label: acute lymphoblastic leukemia
source_fields.definition: Leukemia with an acute onset, characterized by the presence of lymphoblasts in the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. It includes the acute B lymphoblastic leukemia and acute T lymphoblastic leukemia.

source_fields.label: microcytic anemia
source_fields.definition: Anemia in which the red blood cell volume is decreased.

source_fields.label: macrocytic anemia
source_fields.definition: Anemia that is characterized by increased red blood cell volume.

source_fields.label: hypophosphatemia
source_fields.definition: Lower than normal levels of phosphates in the circulating blood.

source_fields.label: rickets
source_fields.definition: Bone softening and weakening usually caused by deficiency or impaired metabolism of vitamin D. Deficiency of calcium, magnesium, or phosphorus may also cause rickets. It predominantly affects children who suffer from severe malnutrition. It manifests with bone pain, fractures, muscle weakness, and skeletal deformities.

source_fields.label: lymphopenia
source_fields.definition: Reduction in the number of lymphocytes.

source_fields.label: anemia
source_fields.definition: A reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells. Clinically, anemia represents a reduction in the oxygen-transporting capacity of a designated volume of blood, resulting from an imbalance between blood loss (through hemorrhage or hemolysis) and blood production. Signs and symptoms of anemia may include pallor of the skin and mucous membranes, shortness of breath, palpitations of the heart, soft systolic murmurs, lethargy, and fatigability.

source_fields.label: lymphoid leukemia
source_fields.definition: A malignant lymphocytic neoplasm of B-cell or T-cell lineage involving primarily the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. This category includes precursor or acute lymphoblastic leukemias and chronic leukemias.

source_fields.label: leukemia
source_fields.definition: A malignant (clonal) hematologic disorder, involving hematopoietic stem cells and characterized by the presence of primitive or atypical myeloid or lymphoid cells in the bone marrow and the blood. Leukemias are classified as acute or chronic based on the degree of cellular differentiation and the predominant cell type present. Leukemia is usually associated with anemia, fever, hemorrhagic episodes, and splenomegaly. Common leukemias include acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia, acute lymphoblastic or precursor lymphoblastic leukemia, and chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Treatment is vital to patient survival; untreated, the natural course of acute leukemias is normally measured in weeks or months, while that of chronic leukemias is more often measured in months or years.

source_fields.label: urinary bladder carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the urinary bladder

source_fields.label: renal cell carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the kidney

source_fields.label: infectious meningitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord caused by an infectious agent (viral, bacterial, or fungal). Symptoms include headache, fever, vomiting, neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, and seizures.

source_fields.label: ichthyosis
source_fields.definition: Disorders of cornification that are characterized by visible scaling and/or hyperkeratosis of most or all of the skin. Inherited ichthyoses, defined as the generalized form of Mendelian disorders of cornification, affect most or all of the skin. This etiologically and phenotypically heterogenous group of conditions is caused by mutations in various different genes important for keratinocyte differentiation and epidermal barrier function. Acquired forms of ichthyosis can be observed with certain autoimmune, inflammatory, metabolic, endocrine, or infectious diseases or with malignancies.

source_fields.label: exanthem
source_fields.definition: A skin disease characterized by widespread, often symmetrical skin eruption that typically occurs acutely in association with a systemic disease, especially infectious or immune-mediated conditions.

source_fields.label: hypercalcemia disease
source_fields.definition: Abnormally high concentration of calcium in the peripheral blood.

source_fields.label: goiter
source_fields.definition: Enlargement of the thyroid gland usually caused by lack of iodine in the diet, hyperthyroidism, or thyroid nodules. Symptoms include difficulty in breathing and swallowing.

source_fields.label: hyperinsulinism
source_fields.definition: Abnormally high levels of insulin in the blood.

source_fields.label: sleep apnea syndrome
source_fields.definition: A disorder characterized by multiple cessations of respirations during sleep that induce partial arousals and interfere with the maintenance of sleep.
synonyms: mixed central and obstructive sleep apnea
sleep apnea, mixed central and obstructive

source_fields.label: canker sore
source_fields.definition: A type of stomatitis that is characterized by small white ulcerative lesions, single or multiple, round or oval, lasting for 7-14 days and healing without scarring. It is a recurrent disease of the oral mucosa of unknown etiology.

source_fields.label: neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant tissue growth resulting from uncontrolled cell proliferation. Benign neoplastic cells resemble normal cells without exhibiting significant cytologic atypia, while malignant cells exhibit overt signs such as dysplastic features, atypical mitotic figures, necrosis, nuclear pleomorphism, and anaplasia. Representative examples of benign neoplasms include papillomas, cystadenomas, and lipomas; malignant neoplasms include carcinomas, sarcomas, lymphomas, and leukemias.

source_fields.label: pericardial effusion
source_fields.definition: Fluid collection within the pericardial sac, usually due to inflammation.

source_fields.label: asthma
source_fields.definition: A bronchial disease that is characterized by chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways, which is caused by a combination of environmental and genetic factors resulting in recurring periods of wheezing (a whistling sound while breathing), chest tightness, shortness of breath, mucus production and coughing. The symptoms appear due to a variety of triggers such as allergens, irritants, respiratory infections, weather changes, exercise, stress, reflux disease, medications, foods and emotional anxiety.
synonyms: chronic obstructive asthma with acute exacerbation
chronic obstructive asthma with status asthmaticus

source_fields.label: constipation disorder
source_fields.definition: Irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels.

source_fields.label: potassium deficiency disease
source_fields.definition: Any disorder caused by an insufficient amount or availability of potassium, which generally manifests with myalgia, tetany, hypotension, polyuria, and polydipsia.

source_fields.label: endometriosis
source_fields.definition: The growth of functional endometrial tissue in anatomic sites outside the uterine body. It most often occurs in the pelvic organs.

source_fields.label: pyuria
source_fields.definition: The presence of excessive white blood cells in the urine as determined by urinalysis.

source_fields.label: urticaria
source_fields.definition: A vascular reaction of the skin characterized by erythema and wheal formation due to localized increase of vascular permeability. The causative mechanism may be allergy, infection, or stress.

source_fields.label: urethral stricture
source_fields.definition: Narrowing of any part of the urethra. It is characterized by decreased urinary stream and often other obstructive voiding symptoms.

source_fields.label: non-small cell lung carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A group of at least three distinct histological types of lung cancer, including non-small cell squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and large cell carcinoma. Non-small cell lung carcinomas have a poor response to conventional chemotherapy.
synonyms: non-small cell cancer of the lung
non-small cell carcinoma of the lung

source_fields.label: hypertriglyceridemia
source_fields.definition: A laboratory test result indicating elevated triglyceride concentration in the blood.

source_fields.label: purpura
source_fields.definition: A small blood vessel hemorrhage into the skin and/or mucous membranes. Newer lesions appear reddish in color. Older lesions are usually a darker purple color and eventually become a brownish-yellow color.

source_fields.label: atrial flutter
source_fields.definition: A disorder characterized by an electrocardiographic finding of an organized, regular atrial rhythm with atrial rate of 240-340 beats per minute. Multiple P waves typically appear in the inferior leads in a saw tooth-like pattern between the QRS complexes. (CDISC)

source_fields.label: pulmonary embolism
source_fields.definition: The obstruction of the pulmonary artery or one of its branches by an embolus, sometimes associated with infarction of the lung.

source_fields.label: colitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the colon.

source_fields.label: acne
source_fields.definition: An inflammatory process of the sebaceous glands which is characterized by comedones, nodules, papules and/or pustules on the skin.

source_fields.label: recurrent pneumonia
source_fields.definition: Infections with nontuberculous mycobacteria (atypical mycobacteria): M. kansasii, M. marinum, M. scrofulaceum, M. flavescens, M. gordonae, M. obuense, M. gilvum, M. duvali, M. szulgai, M. intracellulare (see mycobacterium avium complex;), M. xenopi (littorale), M. ulcerans, M. buruli, M. terrae, M. fortuitum (minetti, giae), M. chelonae.

source_fields.label: cavernous hemangioma
source_fields.definition: A hemangioma characterized by the presence of cavernous vascular spaces.

source_fields.label: lipodystrophy
source_fields.definition: A congenital or acquired disorder characterized by abnormal loss or redistribution of the adipose tissue in the body.

source_fields.label: esophagitis
source_fields.definition: An acute or chronic inflammatory disease affecting the esophageal wall.

source_fields.label: rhabdomyosarcoma
source_fields.definition: A rare aggressive malignant mesenchymal neoplasm arising from skeletal muscle. It usually occurs in children and young adults. Only a small percentage of tumors arise in the skeletal muscle of the extremities. The majority arise in other anatomical sites.

source_fields.label: congenital heart disease
source_fields.definition: A heart disease that is present at birth. Representative examples include atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot, and patent foramen ovale.

source_fields.label: folliculitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the hair follicles. Causes include excessive perspiration, skin infections, and skin wounds.

source_fields.label: brain disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease affecting the brain or part of the brain.

source_fields.label: pulmonary fibrosis
source_fields.definition: Chronic progressive interstitial lung disorder characterized by the replacement of the lung tissue by connective tissue, leading to progressive dyspnea, respiratory failure, or right heart failure. Causes include chronic inflammatory processes, exposure to environmental irritants, radiation therapy, autoimmune disorders, certain drugs, or it may be idiopathic (no identifiable cause).

source_fields.label: lysosomal lipid storage disorder
source_fields.definition: An inherited metabolic disorder in which harmful amounts of lipids accumulate in cells and tissues. Because of a functionally impaired hydrolase or auxiliary protein, their lipid substrates cannot be degraded, accumulate in the lysosome, and slowly spread to other intracellular membranes.
synonyms: rare inborn error of lipid storage

source_fields.label: chorioretinitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the distal posterior uveal tract (choroid) and its structural and vascular attachments to the retina. It is usually caused by infection and though rare, it is clinically significant due to its most serious sequela: loss of vision.

source_fields.label: myopathy
source_fields.definition: A disease of the muscle in which the muscle fibers do not function properly. This results in muscular weakness.

source_fields.label: inherited lipid metabolism disorder
source_fields.definition: An inherited metabolic disorder caused by an enzyme deficiency, resulting in an inability to oxidize fatty acids for energy production.

source_fields.label: adrenogenital syndrome
source_fields.definition: Abnormal sex differentiation or congenital disorders of sex development caused by abnormal levels of steroid hormones expressed by the gonads or the adrenal glands, such as in congenital adrenal hyperplasia and adrenal cortex neoplasms. Due to abnormal steroid biosynthesis, clinical features include virilism in females; feminization in males; or precocious sexual development in children.

source_fields.label: ehrlichiosis
source_fields.definition: An disease or disorder caused by infection with Ehrlichia.

source_fields.label: spotted fever
source_fields.definition: A type of tick-borne disease which presents on the skin caused by bacteria of the genus Rickettsia.

source_fields.label: gastrointestinal anthrax
source_fields.definition: An anthrax disease that results in infection located in mucosa of gastrointestinal tract, has material basis in Bacillus anthracis, which is transmitted by ingestion of anthrax-infected meat. The infection has symptom lesions, has symptom vomiting of blood, has symptom severe diarrhea, has symptom loss of appetite.

source_fields.label: cardiomyopathy
source_fields.definition: A disease of the heart muscle or myocardium proper. Cardiomyopathies may be classified as either primary or secondary, on the basis of etiology, or on the pathophysiology of the lesion: hypertrophic, dilated, or restrictive.

source_fields.label: tinea corporis
source_fields.definition: A dermatophyte disease of the glabrous skin, excluding the scalp, beard, face, hands, feet, and groin.

source_fields.label: gastroenteritis
source_fields.definition: An inflammatory disorder that affects the upper and lower gastrointestinal tract. Most commonly, this is attributed to viruses; however bacteria, parasites or adverse reactions can also be the culprit. Symptoms include acute diarrhea and vomiting.

source_fields.label: fungal infectious disease
source_fields.definition: An infection caused by a fungus.

source_fields.label: tonsillitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the tonsillar tissue.

source_fields.label: nasopharyngitis
source_fields.definition: An inflammatory process that affects the nasopharynx.

source_fields.label: pneumonia
source_fields.definition: An acute, acute and chronic, or chronic inflammation focally or diffusely affecting the lung parenchyma, caused by an infection in one or both of the lungs (by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or mycoplasma.). Symptoms include cough, shortness of breath, fevers, chills, chest pain, headache, sweating, and weakness.

display_name: hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome

source_fields.label: hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome
source_fields.definition: A disorder caused by hantaviruses of the family Bunyaviridae. It is transmitted by rodents and is manifested with fever, hemorrhage, and renal failure. Other symptoms include headaches, abdominal and back pain, and blurred vision.

source_fields.label: liver disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the liver.
synonyms: liver and intrahepatic bile duct disorder

source_fields.label: Enoplea infectious disease
source_fields.definition: Infections with nematodes of the order enoplida.

source_fields.label: parasitic infectious disease
source_fields.definition: A successful invasion of a host by an organism that uses the host for food and shelter.

source_fields.label: phosphorus metabolism disease
source_fields.definition: A metabolic disorder that affects the phosphate homeostasis.

source_fields.label: mycobacterial infectious disease
source_fields.definition: Infection due to organisms from the genus Mycobacteria.

source_fields.label: typhus
source_fields.definition: A group of infectious diseases that include epidemic typhus, scrub typhus and murine typhus.

source_fields.label: neurosyphilis
source_fields.definition: Infection of the brain or spinal cord by Treponema pallidum. It occurs many years following the original infection which remained untreated. Signs and symptoms include abnormal gait, blindness, depression, paralysis, seizures and dementia.

source_fields.label: smallpox
source_fields.definition: A condition that is caused by infection with Variola, and that is characterized by small, raised bumps.
synonyms: Variola virus caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: cancer
source_fields.definition: A tumor composed of atypical neoplastic, often pleomorphic cells that invade other tissues. Malignant neoplasms often metastasize to distant anatomic sites and may recur after excision. The most common malignant neoplasms are carcinomas (adenocarcinomas or squamous cell carcinomas), Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas, leukemias, melanomas, and sarcomas.

source_fields.label: testicular cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the testis. Representative examples include seminoma, embryonal carcinoma, sarcoma, leukemia, and lymphoma.

source_fields.label: benign urinary system neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A non-metastasizing neoplasm that arises from the organs that comprise the urinary system. Representative examples include renal oncocytoma, bladder inverted papilloma, and urothelial papilloma.
synonyms: benign neoplasm of the urinary tract
benign tumor of the urinary tract
benign tumour of the urinary tract

source_fields.label: urinary bladder neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm of the bladder. - 2003

source_fields.label: neuroendocrine carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A malignant neuroendocrine neoplasm composed of cells containing secretory granules that stain positive for NSE and chromogranin. The neoplastic cells are often round and form clusters or trabecular sheets. Representative examples are small cell carcinoma, large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma.

source_fields.label: omphalitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the umbilical cord stump in newborns.

source_fields.label: epilepsy
source_fields.definition: A brain disorder characterized by episodes of abnormally increased neuronal discharge resulting in transient episodes of sensory or motor neurological dysfunction, or psychic dysfunction. These episodes may or may not be associated with loss of consciousness or convulsions.

source_fields.label: vitamin B12 deficiency
source_fields.definition: A disease characterized by low serum levels of vitamin B12, either inherited or acquired.

source_fields.label: B-cell neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A group of heterogeneous lymphoid tumors generally expressing one or more B-cell antigens or representing malignant transformations of B-lymphocytes.

source_fields.label: heart conduction disease
source_fields.definition: A disease that has its basis in the disruption of the heart's electrical conduction system.

source_fields.label: vitamin deficiency disorder
source_fields.definition: A disorder that is caused by the deficiency of a vitamin. The deficiency may result from either suboptimal vitamin intake or conditions that prevent the vitamin's use or absorption in the body. Representative examples include beriberi caused by thiamine deficiency, scurvy caused by vitamin C deficiency, and rickets caused by vitamin D deficiency.

source_fields.label: disorder of orbital region
source_fields.definition: A disease that involves the orbital region.
synonyms: disease or disorder of orbital region

source_fields.label: heart disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the heart and/or pericardium.

source_fields.label: heart valve disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the cardial valve.
synonyms: disease or disorder of cardial valve

source_fields.label: vascular disorder
source_fields.definition: A general term used to describe any disease affecting blood vessels]. It includes vascular abnormalities caused by degenerative, metabolic and inflammatory conditions, embolic diseases, coagulative disorders, and functional disorders such as posteri or reversible encephalopathy syndrome.

source_fields.label: skeletal muscle disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the skeletal muscle tissue.
synonyms: disease or disorder of skeletal muscle tissue
skeletal muscle tissue disease or disorder

source_fields.label: cystitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the urinary bladder.

source_fields.label: intellectual disability
source_fields.definition: A broad category of disorders characterized by an impairment to the intelligence an individual possesses. These impairments can result from trauma, birth, or disease and are not restricted to any particular age group.

source_fields.label: metastatic melanoma
source_fields.definition: A melanoma that has spread from its primary site to another anatomic site. Melanomas frequently metastasize to lymph nodes, liver, lungs, and brain.

source_fields.label: malignant epithelial tumor of ovary
source_fields.definition: An invasive malignant tumor that originates from the surface epithelium of the ovary. It is composed of malignant epithelial cells and stroma. Representative examples include serous adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenocarcinoma, endometrioid adenocarcinoma, clear cell adenocarcinoma, and malignant Brenner tumor.

source_fields.label: sympathetic paraganglioma
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant paraganglioma arising from the chromaffin cells of the paraganglia that are located along the sympathetic nerves. It includes extra-adrenal paragangliomas and paragangliomas that arise from the adrenal medulla. The latter are commonly referred to as pheochromocytomas. Representative examples of extra-adrenal sympathetic paragangliomas include the bladder, and superior and inferior paraaortic paragangliomas. Clinical signs are related to the secretion of catecholamines resulting in hypertension.

source_fields.label: endometrial carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A malignant tumor arising from the epithelium that lines the cavity of the uterine body. The vast majority of endometrial carcinomas are adenocarcinomas; squamous cell and adenosquamous carcinomas represent a minority of the cases. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most frequently seen variant of endometrial adenocarcinoma. Uterine bleeding is an initial clinical sign. The prognosis depends on the stage of the tumor, the depth of myometrial wall invasion, and the degree of differentiation.

source_fields.label: uterine corpus cancer
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the body of uterus.
synonyms: malignant neoplasm of body of uterus

source_fields.label: cervical adenocarcinoma
source_fields.definition: An adenocarcinoma arising from the cervical epithelium. It accounts for approximately 15% of invasive cervical carcinomas. Increased numbers of sexual partners and human papillomavirus (HPV) infection are risk factors. Grossly, advanced cervical adenocarcinoma may present as an exophytic mass, an ulcerated lesion, or diffuse cervical enlargement. Microscopically, the majority of cervical adenocarcinomas are of the endocervical (mucinous) type.

source_fields.label: central nervous system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the central nervous system.
synonyms: central nervous system disease or disorder
disease of the central nervous system
disease or disorder of central nervous system

source_fields.label: severe combined immunodeficiency
source_fields.definition: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) comprises a group of rare monogenic primary immunodeficiency disorders characterized by a lack of functional peripheral T lymphocytes resulting in early-onset severe respiratory infections and failure to thrive. They are classified according to immunological phenotype into SCID with absence of T cells but presence of B cells (T-B+ SCID) or SCID with absence of both (T-B- SCID). Both of these groups include several forms, with or without natural killer (NK) cells.

source_fields.label: digestive system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease or disorder that involves the digestive system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of digestive system

source_fields.label: musculoskeletal system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the musculoskeletal system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of musculoskeletal system

source_fields.label: peripheral nervous system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the peripheral nervous system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of peripheral nervous system
disorder of the peripheral nervous system
peripheral nervous system disease or disorder

source_fields.label: learning disability
source_fields.definition: A group of disorders that affect a person's ability to learn or process specific types of information which is in contrast to his/her apparent level of intellect.

source_fields.label: hematologic disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the hematopoietic system.
synonyms: disease of the blood and blood-forming organs
disease or disorder of haematopoietic system
disease or disorder of hematopoietic system

source_fields.label: cardiovascular disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the cardiovascular system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of cardiovascular system

source_fields.label: immune system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disorder resulting from an abnormality in the immune system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of immune system

source_fields.label: kidney disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the kidney.

source_fields.label: blood coagulation disease
source_fields.definition: A condition in which there is a deviation from or interruption of the normal coagulation properties of the blood.

source_fields.label: thrombotic disease
source_fields.definition: The formation of a blood clot in the lumen of a vessel or heart chamber; causes include coagulation disorders and vascular endothelial injury.

source_fields.label: lymphatic system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the lymphatic part of lymphoid system.
synonyms: disease of lymphatic part of lymphoid system
disease or disorder of lymphatic part of lymphoid system
disorder of lymphatic part of lymphoid system
lymphatic part of lymphoid system disease
lymphatic part of lymphoid system disease or disorder

source_fields.label: breast neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm of the breast parenchyma. It can originate from the ducts, lobules or the breast adipose tissue. Breast neoplasms are much more common in females than males.

source_fields.label: female reproductive system neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign, precancerous, or malignant neoplasm that affects the female reproductive system. Representative examples include uterine corpus leiomyoma, endocervical polyp, ovarian carcinoma, cervical carcinoma, and endometrial carcinoma.
synonyms: neoplasm of the female reproductive system
tumor of the female reproductive system
tumour of the female reproductive system

source_fields.label: central nervous system neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. Representative examples of primary neoplasms include astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma, and meningioma. Representative examples of metastatic neoplasms include carcinoma and leukemia.
synonyms: neoplasm of the central nervous system
tumor of the central nervous system
tumour of the central nervous system

source_fields.label: glioma
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant brain and spinal cord tumor that arises from glial cells (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, ependymal cells). Tumors that arise from astrocytes are called astrocytic tumors or astrocytomas. Tumors that arise from oligodendrocytes are called oligodendroglial tumors. Tumors that arise from ependymal cells are called ependymomas.

source_fields.label: obsolete cartilage disease
source_fields.definition: OBSOLETE. Softening and degeneration of the CARTILAGE. Pathological processes involving the chondral tissue (CARTILAGE).
synonyms: disease or disorder of cartilage tissue

source_fields.label: central nervous system cancer
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the central nervous system
synonyms: cancer of the central nervous system
malignant neoplasm of central nervous system
malignant neoplasm of the central nervous system
malignant tumor of central nervous system
malignant tumor of the central nervous system
malignant tumour of central nervous system
malignant tumour of the central nervous system

source_fields.label: brain neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A neoplasm (disease) that involves the brain.

source_fields.label: neuromuscular disease
source_fields.definition: Any disease that impairs the functioning of the muscles, either directly, being pathologies of the voluntary muscle, or indirectly, being pathologies of nerves or neuromuscular junctions.

source_fields.label: vision disorder
source_fields.definition: Any impairment to the vision.

source_fields.label: duodenitis
source_fields.definition: Acute or chronic inflammation of the duodenum. Causes include bacterial and viral infections and gastroesophageal reflux disease. Symptoms include vomiting and abdominal pain.

source_fields.label: eye disorder
source_fields.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the eye. Representative examples include conjunctivitis, glaucoma, cataract, conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma, uveal melanoma, and retinoblastoma.
synonyms: disease of eyeball of camera-type eye
disease or disorder of eyeball of camera-type eye
disorder of eyeball of camera-type eye
eyeball of camera-type eye disease or disorder

source_fields.label: corneal disorder
source_fields.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the cornea. Representative examples include keratitis, bullous keratopathy, and squamous cell carcinoma.

source_fields.label: upper respiratory tract disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the upper respiratory tract.
synonyms: disease or disorder of upper respiratory tract
upper respiratory tract disease or disorder

source_fields.label: respiratory tract infectious disorder
source_fields.definition: Invasion of the host RESPIRATORY SYSTEM by microorganisms, usually leading to pathological processes or diseases.

source_fields.label: lung disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the lung.

source_fields.label: tooth disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the calcareous tooth.
synonyms: disease or disorder of calcareous tooth

source_fields.label: bartonellosis
source_fields.definition: An infectious disease produced by bacteria of the genus Bartonella.

source_fields.label: peripheral neuropathy
source_fields.definition: A disorder affecting the peripheral nervous system. It manifests with pain, tingling, numbness, and muscle weakness. It may be the result of physical injury, toxic substances, viral diseases, diabetes, renal failure, cancer, and drugs.

source_fields.label: bone disorder
source_fields.definition: Diseases of bones.
synonyms: disease or disorder of bone element

source_fields.label: retinitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the retina.

source_fields.label: cytomegalovirus infection
source_fields.definition: A herpesvirus infection caused by Cytomegalovirus. Healthy individuals generally do not produce symptoms. However, the infection may be life-threatening in affected immunocompromised patients. The virus may cause retinitis, esophagitis, gastritis, and colitis. Morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of intranuclear inclusion bodies.

source_fields.label: viral eye infection
source_fields.definition: Infections of the eye caused by minute intracellular agents. These infections may lead to severe inflammation in various parts of the eye - conjunctiva, iris, eyelids, etc. Several viruses have been identified as the causative agents. Among these are Herpesvirus, Adenovirus, Poxvirus, and Myxovirus.

source_fields.label: candidiasis
source_fields.definition: Infection with the organism Candida.

source_fields.label: bacterial meningitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord due to a bacterial infection.

source_fields.label: duodenum cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the duodenum. Representative examples include carcinoma, lymphoma, and sarcoma.

source_fields.label: small intestine cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the small intestine.
synonyms: malignant neoplasm of the small bowel
malignant neoplasm of the small intestine
malignant neoplasms of the small intestine
malignant tumor of the small bowel
malignant tumor of the small intestine
malignant tumour of the small bowel
malignant tumour of the small intestine

source_fields.label: pulmonary emphysema
source_fields.definition: A subcategory of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It occurs in people who smoke and suffer from chronic bronchitis. It is characterized by inflation of the alveoli, alveolar wall damage, and reduction in the number of alveoli, resulting in difficulty breathing.

source_fields.label: leiomyoma
source_fields.definition: A well-circumscribed benign smooth muscle neoplasm characterized by the presence of spindle cells with cigar-shaped nuclei, interlacing fascicles, and a whorled pattern.

source_fields.label: Treponema infectious disease
source_fields.definition: An disease caused by infection with Treponema.

display_name: bacterial meningitis caused by gram-negative bacteria

source_fields.label: bacterial meningitis caused by gram-negative bacteria
synonyms: bacterial meningitis caused by gram-negative bacteria
bacterial meningitis due to gram-negative bacteria

source_fields.label: central nervous system infectious disorder
source_fields.definition: An infectious process that affects the brain and/or spinal cord. Representative examples include encephalitis, poliomyelitis, arachnoiditis, and meningitis.
synonyms: infectious disease of central nervous system

source_fields.label: cerebrovascular disorder
source_fields.definition: A disorder resulting from inadequate blood flow in the vessels that supply the brain. Representative examples include cerebrovascular ischemia, cerebral embolism, and cerebral infarction.

source_fields.label: sexual disorder
source_fields.definition: A category of psychiatric disorders characterized by a disturbance in sexual desire and in the psychophysiological changes that make up the sexual response cycle.

source_fields.label: mental disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease that has its basis in the disruption of mental process.

source_fields.label: dry eye syndrome
source_fields.definition: A syndrome characterized by dryness of the cornea and conjunctiva. It is usually caused by a deficiency in tear production. Symptoms include a feeling of burning eyes and a possible foreign body presence in the eye.

source_fields.label: optic papillitis
source_fields.definition: Swelling of the optic disk, usually in association with increased intracranial pressure, characterized by hyperemia, blurring of the disk margins, microhemorrhages, blind spot enlargement, and engorgement of retinal veins. Chronic papilledema may cause optic atrophy and visual loss. (Miller et al., Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology, 4th ed, p175)
synonyms: papilledema associated with decreased intraocular pressure
papilledema associated with increased intracranial pressure

source_fields.label: neuritis
source_fields.definition: A neuropathy arising from inflammation of one or more nerves.

source_fields.label: peripheral vascular disease
source_fields.definition: Any disorder affecting blood flow through the veins or arteries outside of the heart.

source_fields.label: atherosclerosis
source_fields.definition: A disease characterized by the build-up of fatty material and calcium deposition in the arterial wall resulting in partial or complete occlusion of the arterial lumen.

source_fields.label: pericarditis
source_fields.definition: An inflammatory process affecting the pericardium.

source_fields.label: histoplasmosis
source_fields.definition: A disease caused by the fungus Histoplasma capsulatum. It primarily affects the lungs but can also occur as a disseminated disease that affects additional organs. The acute respiratory disease has symptoms similar to those of a cold or flu and it usually resolves without treatment in healthy individuals. The disseminated form is generally fatal if untreated.

source_fields.label: auditory system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the auditory system.
synonyms: disease or disorder of auditory system

source_fields.label: prostate carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the prostate gland.

source_fields.label: malignant urinary system neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant tumor involving the urinary system. Common tumor types include carcinomas, lymphomas, and sarcomas.

source_fields.label: prostate cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant tumor involving the prostate gland. The vast majority are carcinomas.

source_fields.label: lymphoma
source_fields.definition: A malignant (clonal) proliferation of B- lymphocytes or T- lymphocytes which involves the lymph nodes, bone marrow and/or extranodal sites. This category includes Non-Hodgkin lymphomas and Hodgkin lymphomas.

source_fields.label: esotropia
source_fields.definition: A form of strabismus in which one or both eyes are deviated medially.

source_fields.label: meningitis
source_fields.definition: A disorder characterized by acute inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord.

source_fields.label: amblyopia
source_fields.definition: Decreased vision that results from abnormal visual development.

source_fields.label: gonorrhea
source_fields.definition: A common sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. It is transmitted through vaginal, oral, or anal intercourse. Infected individuals may be asymptomatic. Symptoms in males include burning sensation during urination, discharge from the penis, and painful swelling of the testes. Symptoms in females include painful urination, vaginal discharge, and vaginal bleeding between periods. If untreated, the infection may lead to pelvic inflammatory disease.

source_fields.label: infectious anterior uveitis
source_fields.definition: An infectious disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the anterior uvea.

source_fields.label: tendinitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of a tendon, usually resulting from an overuse injury. It is characterized by swelling of the tendon, tenderness around the inflamed tendon, and pain while moving the affected area of the body.

source_fields.label: esophageal disorder
source_fields.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the esophagus. Representative examples of non-neoplastic disorders include esophagitis and esophageal ulcer. Representative examples of neoplastic disorders include carcinomas, lymphomas, and melanomas.

source_fields.label: intestinal disorder
source_fields.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the small or large intestine.

source_fields.label: anus disorder
source_fields.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the anal canal or anal margin. Representative examples of non-neoplastic disorders include hemorrhoids and anal ulcer. Representative examples of neoplastic disorders include carcinoma, lymphoma, and melanoma.

source_fields.label: gastric neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm involving the stomach.

source_fields.label: gastric adenocarcinoma
source_fields.definition: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the stomach

source_fields.label: yaws
source_fields.definition: An endemic, infectious, nonvenereal disease in humans that presents mainly in children younger than 15 years. The disease occurs primarily in warm, humid, tropical areas of Africa, Asia, South America, and Oceania, among poor rural populations where conditions of overcrowding and poor sanitation prevail. Infection with Treponema pertenue, a subspecies of Treponema pallidum, causes the disease.
synonyms: Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue caused disease or disorder
Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue disease or disorder
Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue infectious disease

source_fields.label: tic disorder
source_fields.definition: Disorders characterized by recurrent TICS that may interfere with speech and other activities. Tics are sudden, rapid, nonrhythmic, stereotyped motor movements or vocalizations which may be exacerbated by stress and are generally attenuated during absorbing activities. Tic disorders are distinguished from conditions which feature other types of abnormal movements that may accompany another another condition. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

source_fields.label: cervicitis
source_fields.definition: An acute or chronic inflammatory process that affects the cervix. Causes include sexually transmitted diseases and bacterial infections. Clinical manifestations include abnormal vaginal bleeding and vaginal discharge.

source_fields.label: nephritis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of renal tissue.

source_fields.label: lymphangioma
source_fields.definition: A benign lesion composed of dilated lymphatic channels. Painless swelling is the usual clinical manifestation.

source_fields.label: open-angle glaucoma
source_fields.definition: Chronic outflow obstruction of the eye's drainage canals that can lead to increased internal eye pressure and optic nerve damage.

source_fields.label: hyperthyroidism
source_fields.definition: Overactivity of the thyroid gland resulting in overproduction of thyroid hormone and increased metabolic rate. Causes include diffuse hyperplasia of the thyroid gland (Graves' disease), single nodule in the thyroid gland, and thyroiditis. The symptoms are related to the increased metabolic rate and include weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, diarrhea, tachycardia, insomnia, muscle weakness, and tremor.

source_fields.label: chronic kidney disease
source_fields.definition: Impairment of the renal function secondary to chronic kidney damage persisting for three or more months.

source_fields.label: myocarditis
source_fields.definition: Myocarditis is a condition that is characterized by inflammation of the heart muscle (myocardium). Some affected people have no noticeable symptoms of the condition. When present, signs and symptoms may include chest pain, abnormal heartbeat, shortness of breath, fatigue, signs of infection (i.e. fever, headache, sore throat, diarrhea), and leg swelling. Myocarditis can be caused by a variety of factors including infections (viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal), allergic reactions to certain medications, and exposure to certain chemicals. It can also be associated with other inflammatory conditions such as lupus, Wegener's granulomatosis, giant cell arteritis and Takayasu's arteritis. Most cases occur sporadically in people with no family history of the condition. Treatment aims to address the underlying cause of the condition. Medications and rarely, a heart transplant may be needed if the heart muscle becomes weak.

source_fields.label: sinusitis
source_fields.definition: An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the mucous membranes of any sinus cavity.

source_fields.label: peptic ulcer disease
source_fields.definition: A digestive system disease characterized by discontinuation in the inner lining of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract because of gastric acid secretion or pepsin.
synonyms: acute peptic ulcer with haemorrhage and perforation
acute peptic ulcer without haemorrhage and without perforation

source_fields.label: head and neck cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm affecting the head and neck. Representative examples include oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, and salivary gland carcinoma.
synonyms: cancer of the head and neck
malignant neoplasm of head and neck
malignant neoplasm of the head and neck
malignant tumor of head and neck
malignant tumor of the head and neck
malignant tumour of head and neck
malignant tumour of the head and neck

source_fields.label: thrombophlebitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the veins associated with the presence of a thrombus.
synonyms: phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of superficial vessels of lower extremities

source_fields.label: cognitive disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease affects cognitive processes.

source_fields.label: palsy
source_fields.definition: A general term most often used to describe severe or complete loss of muscle strength due to motor system disease from the level of the cerebral cortex to the muscle fiber. This term may also occasionally refer to a loss of sensory function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p45)

source_fields.label: oophoritis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the ovary, generally caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix.

source_fields.label: soft tissue sarcoma
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm arising from muscle tissue, adipose tissue, blood vessels, fibrous tissue, or other supportive tissues excluding the bones.

source_fields.label: respiratory failure
source_fields.definition: The significant impairment of gas exchange within the lungs resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both, to the extent that organ tissue perfusion is severely compromised. Causes include chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, emphysema, acute respiratory distress syndrome, pneumonia, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, and congestive heart failure. Treatment requires intubation and mechanical ventilation until the time the lungs recover sufficient function.

source_fields.label: atopic conjunctivitis
source_fields.definition: Conjunctivitis due to hypersensitivity to various allergens.

source_fields.label: neutropenia
source_fields.definition: A decrease in the number of neutrophils found in the blood.

source_fields.label: phobic disorder
source_fields.definition: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of an object, activity, or situation. The individual seeks to avoid the object, activity, or situation. In adults, the individual recognizes that the fear is excessive or unreasonable.

source_fields.label: chlamydia trachomatis infectious disease
source_fields.definition: An infection that is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis.
synonyms: Chlamydia trachomatis caused disease or disorder

source_fields.label: schistosomiasis
source_fields.definition: An infectious disease caused by parasitic trematodes of the genus Schistosoma that colonize human blood vessels and release eggs that can cause granulomatous reactions leading to acute (swimmer's itch or acute schistosomiasis syndrome) or chronic disease. Depending on where the eggs lodge, manifestations of chronic schistosomiasis can include diarrhea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, anemia (intestines), hepatosplenism, periportal fibrosis with portal hypertension (liver), urogenital inflammation and scarring, hematuria and dysuria (genitourinary system). Other patients may be asymptomatic.

source_fields.label: fungal infection of eye
source_fields.definition: Infection by a variety of fungi, usually through four possible mechanisms: superficial infection producing conjunctivitis, keratitis, or lacrimal obstruction; extension of infection from neighboring structures - skin, paranasal sinuses, nasopharynx; direct introduction during surgery or accidental penetrating trauma; or via the blood or lymphatic routes in patients with underlying mycoses.

source_fields.label: streptococcal infection
source_fields.definition: Any of the several infectious disorders caused by members of streptococcus, a genus of gram positive bacteria belonging to the family Streptococcaceae. Streptococcal infections are classified into Groups A, B, C, D and G.

source_fields.label: lens disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the lens of camera-type eye.
synonyms: disease of lens of camera-type eye
disease or disorder of lens of camera-type eye
disorder of lens of camera-type eye
lens of camera-type eye disease or disorder

source_fields.label: vasculitis
source_fields.definition: Vasculitis represents a clinically heterogenous group of diseases of multifactorial etiology characterized by inflammation of either large-sized vessels (large-vessel vasculitis, e.g. Giant-cell arteritis and Takayasu arteritis), medium-sized vessels (medium-vessel vasculitis e.g. polyarteritis nodosa and Kawasaki disease), or small-sized vessels (small-vessel vasculitis, e.g. granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis, immunoglobulin A vasculitis, and cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis). Vasculitis occurs at any age, may be acute or chronic, and manifests with general symptoms such as fever, weight loss and fatigue, as well as more specific clinical signs depending on the type of vessels and organs affected. The degree of severity is variable, ranging from life or sight threatening disease (e.g. Behcet disease) to relatively minor skin disease.

source_fields.label: atopic eczema
source_fields.definition: A common chronic pruritic inflammatory skin disease with a strong genetic component. Onset typically occurs during the first 2 years of life.

source_fields.label: hypersensitivity vasculitis
source_fields.definition: A small vessel vasculitis affecting the skin and/or internal organs. It is characterized by the presence of neutrophils and fibrinoid necrosis in small arteries and venules. It may be idiopathic or the result of drug treatment, infections, food intake, collagen vascular disorders, inflammatory bowel disease, or cancer.

source_fields.label: cutaneous vasculitis
source_fields.definition: Inflammation of the blood vessel wall characterized by palpable purpura.

source_fields.label: autonomic nervous system disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the autonomic nervous system.
synonyms: autonomic nervous system disease or disorder
disease or disorder of autonomic nervous system
disorder of peripheral autonomic nervous system
disorder of the autonomic nervous system
disorders of the autonomic nervous system

source_fields.label: arthritic joint disease
source_fields.definition: An inflammatory process affecting a joint. Causes include infection, autoimmune processes, degenerative processes, and trauma. Signs and symptoms may include swelling around the affected joint and pain.

source_fields.label: heart cancer
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the heart

source_fields.label: gynecomastia disorder
source_fields.definition: Development of breast tissue in males.
synonyms: hypertrophy of breast of male organism

source_fields.label: penile neoplasm
source_fields.definition: A benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm that affects the penis. Representative examples include penile hemangioma, penile intraepithelial neoplasia, and penile carcinoma.

source_fields.label: rheumatic disorder
source_fields.definition: Inflammatory and degenerative diseases of connective tissue structures, such as arthritis.

source_fields.label: peritoneum cancer
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the peritoneum

source_fields.label: hemosiderosis
source_fields.definition: Accumulation of iron in internal organs.

source_fields.label: lower respiratory tract disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the lower respiratory tract.
synonyms: disease or disorder of lower respiratory tract
lower respiratory tract disease or disorder

source_fields.label: splenic disorder
source_fields.definition: A disease involving the spleen.

display_name: disease of neck of urinary bladder

source_fields.label: disorder of neck of urinary bladder
synonyms: functional disorder of bladder neck and sphincter mechanism

source_fields.label: blindness (disorder)
source_fields.definition: The lack of vision. It is caused by neurological or physiological factors.

source_fields.label: penile cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the penis. Representative examples include penile carcinoma and penile sarcoma.

source_fields.label: coronary artery disorder
source_fields.definition: Narrowing of the coronary arteries due to fatty deposits inside the arterial walls. The diagnostic criteria may include documented history of any of the following: documented coronary artery stenosis greater than or equal to 50% (by cardiac catheterization or other modality of direct imaging of the coronary arteries); previous coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG); previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); previous myocardial infarction. (ACC)
synonyms: disease or disorder of coronary artery

source_fields.label: female breast carcinoma
source_fields.definition: A carcinoma that arises from the breast in females. It is the most common malignant tumor that affects females.
synonyms: mammary carcinoma of the female breast

source_fields.label: female reproductive organ cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the female reproductive system. Representative examples include endometrial carcinoma, cervical carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, uterine corpus leiomyosarcoma, adenosarcoma, malignant mixed mesodermal (mullerian) tumor, and gestational choriocarcinoma.
synonyms: malignant neoplasm of female reproductive organ
malignant neoplasm of female reproductive system
malignant neoplasm of the female reproductive system
malignant tumor of female reproductive system
malignant tumor of the female reproductive system
malignant tumour of female reproductive system
malignant tumour of the female reproductive system

source_fields.label: vulva cancer
source_fields.definition: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the vulva.

source_fields.label: skin cancer
source_fields.definition: A malignant neoplasm involving the zone of skin
